rationale: R8A0 supplies an unusually clean positive-and-negative case for semantic interface fidelity. An operational interface silently changed accepted truth-class semantics and was explicitly rejected; a later exact Clarification contract was independently approved after the mapping was repaired. I therefore retain SEMANTIC_INTERFACE_FIDELITY as a current Semantic Atlas method: structural translation is allowed, but semantic reclassification must be explicit, traceable, and separately adjudicable rather than hidden inside a field rename or schema rewrite.

SILENT_SEMANTIC_TRANSLATION is retained as a named failure mode because the R8 alignment defect shows why lexical or structural validity is not enough: a representation can remain syntactically coherent while silently changing the governing semantic class. This failure mode is distinct from explicit refinement or correction, which acknowledges the semantic change and preserves lineage.
